        free[m] = (f_cpu, f_mem)
    return free

def can_fit(m, cpu_req, mem_req, time):
    if machines[m]['down']:

    f_cpu, f_mem = get_free_resources(time)[m]
    return f_cpu >= cpu_req and f_mem >= mem_req

    def sort_key(tid):

        s = tasks[tid]['submitted']
        # Lower task id means earlier in sort, so we use tid directly (T001 < T002)
        return (-p, s, tid)
    return sorted(task_list, key=sort_key)

def try_first_fit(task_id):

    t = tasks[task_id]

    return None

def try_preemption(task_id):
    """Try to preempt free-tier tasks from one machine"""
    t = tasks[task_id]
    if t['priority'] < 9:  # Only production tasks (9-11) can preempt

        free_mem = machines[m]['mem'] - ml['mem_used']

        # lowest priority first, then most recently started first, then higher task id first
        ft_tasks = [(tid, end) for tid, end in ml['tasks'] if tasks[tid]['priority'] <= 1]
        
        # Sort: lowest priority first (ascending), then most recently started (descending end time... no, started time)
        # "lowest priority first, then the most recently started first (then the higher task id first)"
        # We need started time - we can compute it as end_time - run_time
        def evict_sort_key(item):
            tid, end = item
            sp = tasks[tid]['priority']
            started = end - tasks[tid]['run_time']
            # Lower priority first -> ascending priority
            # Most recently started first -> descending started time
            # Higher task id first -> descending task id
            return (sp, -started, [-int(tid[1:])])  # hack for descending task id
